title: I made a finnicky mobile online retro turn-based JRPG inspired by the game systems I played as a kid
author: luke_fq
selftext:
TL;DR: I made a game you can play - [click here](http://play.finni.quest)

I've always been more of a systems guy than a story guy. When I played FF/DQ as a kid I spent more time figuring out how damage worked than following the plot, and that never really went away. Job systems, type charts, weird stat interactions, that's the stuff I remember from every game I loved

So for the last few months I've been building my own: finniquest, a free pixel JRPG that runs in the browser. It borrows from a lot of games, but mostly from JRPGs:

Jobs you swap between, FF5 style. Some normal ones (Paladin, Ninja, Wizard) and some that are frankly ridiculous (Accountant, Sysadmin, Tea Master). Clearing a zone unlocks its job.

Every fight is one of your heroes against one monster, and you can switch mid-fight like Pokémon. You pick every move, no auto battler. 

Elements work like a type chart, but the game doesn’t telegraph what's weak to what. You find out when a hit lands and the big red "!" pops up. I really wanted that feeling of learning the chart yourself.

No MP and no cooldowns. Instead, abilities cost TP, which you regain by using basic attacks. It turned out to make every turn a small decision, which I like a lot more than "wait 3 turns", and it is also better suited to the intended faster pace of the game.

There's also an endless dungeon with leaderboards, a daily faction war over the map, and yes, a bonsai you have to water. Don't ask, it made sense at the time.

It's in alpha playtest right now, so things will be rough in places. You can play as a guest, no sign-up needed: play.finni.quest

Always open to feedback, thoughts and ideas on new functions. We also have a Discord.
